transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because at work I keep losing my train of thought. I’m a nurse, and on the floor, if an IV pump starts beeping or someone asks a question nearby or a call light goes off, I’ll suddenly forget what patient flow issue I was in the middle of handling. It’s been happening a lot, and it’s getting really hard to manage.
Have you noticed this kind of distractibility and trouble staying focused going back to childhood or your school years, or is this a new problem that's started more recently?

It’s definitely not new. I remember it being there even in elementary school. Teachers would say I was bright, but careless, and I was always losing worksheets or forgetting to turn in homework. My mom basically had to sit with me every night to keep me on track.

Aside from getting distracted, do you find yourself worrying excessively about multiple different things—like your health, finances, or family—more days than not, even when there's no clear reason to worry?

Not really, no. I mean, I worry about normal life stuff sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying all the time about a bunch of different things for no reason. That doesn’t feel like the main issue for me.
How would you describe your sleep lately—are you getting enough hours and feeling rested when you wake up, or do you notice things like snoring, gasping, or excessive daytime sleepiness?

I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really noticed snoring or gasping, and I don’t think sleep is the main problem. My schedule can be all over the place with work, but I don’t have a clear pattern to point to.
Over the past two weeks, have you noticed a persistent low mood or a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed a consistent low mood, and I still do enjoy things when I can actually get to them. I wouldn’t say that’s been the main thing over the past couple weeks.
Growing up and even now, have you often felt restless, fidgety, or like you needed to be constantly moving or 'on the go,' or found yourself acting impulsively without thinking things through?

I’m not really sure I’d describe myself that way. I don’t think I’m constantly restless or needing to move all the time. And I can’t think of a clear pattern of acting impulsively without thinking—at least nothing that stands out to me.

latest_inference.note: Excluded GAD (patient denies excessive multi-domain worry), depression (no persistent low mood/anhedonia), sleep apnea/insomnia (no snoring, gasping, or clear sleep-related pattern, and symptoms clearly predate any sleep issue), and hyperactive/impulsive subtype (patient denies restlessness or impulsivity). Remaining presentation is a lifelong, childhood-onset pattern of inattention and distractibility consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation.
